questions.title: Section A (Compulsory) - Multiple Choice, Matching Items, and Give the Term

subQuestions.questionText: The actual expenditure that a business incurs in the production process is known as â€¦ costs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - explicit (2 marks)
Explicit costs are the actual monetary payments made by a business for resources used in production.

subQuestions.questionText: The market structure that is regarded as a hybrid structure is known as ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - monopolistic competition (2 marks)
Monopolistic competition is considered a hybrid market structure as it combines features of both monopoly (product differentiation) and perfect competition (many sellers and free entry).

subQuestions.questionText: Most markets fail to adjust rapidly to changes in supply and demand due to a lack of â€¦
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - information (2 marks)
Lack of perfect information about prices and market conditions causes market failure as buyers and sellers cannot make fully informed decisions.

subQuestions.questionText: Black markets develop when the government intervenes by imposing a/an â€¦ price.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - maximum (2 marks)
When government imposes a maximum price (price ceiling) below the equilibrium price, shortages develop, leading to black markets where goods are sold illegally above the maximum price.

subQuestions.questionText: The calculation of the inflation rate of all final goods and services by using the implicit GDP deflator is referred to as â€¦ inflation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - all-inclusive (2 marks)
All-inclusive inflation uses the implicit GDP deflator to measure inflation across all final goods and services in the economy.

subQuestions.questionText: Cost-push inflation will result in â€¦
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - lower profit margins (2 marks)
Cost-push inflation increases production costs, which reduces profit margins for businesses if they cannot fully pass on the higher costs to consumers.

subQuestions.questionText: The minimum length of stay should be â€¦ when measuring tourism.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - one night (2 marks)
For a person to be classified as a tourist, the minimum length of stay is one night away from their usual environment.

subQuestions.questionText: Financial support provided by the government to encourage investment in green energy, is known as a/an â€¦ subsidy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - environmental (2 marks)
Environmental subsidies are financial incentives provided by government to encourage investment in environmentally friendly initiatives such as green/renewable energy.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the term 'Industry' with the correct description from Column B.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: F - a group of businesses that produce or supply similar products (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Match the term 'Natural monopolies' with the correct description from Column B.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the term 'Minimum wage' with the correct description from Column B.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: I - the amount of money set by the government, below which no employer may pay their workers (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Match the term 'Indexes' with the correct description from Column B.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: G - compiled by regularly recording the prices of a representative basket of goods and services (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Match the term 'Outbound tourists' with the correct description from Column B.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: B - South African citizens travelling to other countries (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Match the term 'Sho't left campaign' with the correct description from Column B.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C - aimed at making travelling more accessible and affordable within South Africa (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Match the term 'Millennium Development Goal' with the correct description from Column B.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D - an objective to eradicate extreme poverty and hunger (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE term: Products that are identical in terms of quality, size and appearance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Homogeneous (1 mark)
Homogeneous products are identical/uniform across all suppliers in a market, a key feature of perfect competition.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE term: A legal and exclusive right to manufacture a product.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Patent (1 mark)
A patent is a legal protection granting the inventor exclusive rights to manufacture and sell their invention for a specified period.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE term: A technique for evaluating the social cost and social benefits associated with large government projects.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Cost benefit analysis (1 mark)
Cost-benefit analysis is used to evaluate whether the social benefits of a project outweigh the social costs.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE term: Occurs when there is an increase in the general price level caused by an increase in the cost of production.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Cost-push inflation (1 mark)
Cost-push inflation arises when rising production costs (e.g. wages, raw materials) push up general price levels.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE term: Tourist activities in which people visit places where they can experience the diverse natural beauty of a country.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Ecotourism (1 mark)
Ecotourism involves responsible travel to natural areas to enjoy and experience nature while conserving the environment.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE term: Resources that cannot be replaced once they have been extracted.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Non-renewable resources (1 mark)
Non-renewable resources (e.g. coal, oil, natural gas) cannot be replaced within a human timeframe once consumed.

subQuestions.questionText: Name any TWO features (characteristics) of public goods.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark per correct feature (max 2 marks):
â€¢ Non-rivalry
â€¢ Non-excludable
â€¢ Non-rejectable

(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Why does the kinked demand curve discourage an oligopoly firm from raising its prices?
subQuestions.memoText:
A smaller increase in price may result in a bigger decrease in the quantity demanded which will lower income (total revenue), due to the elastic section of the kinked demand curve. (2 marks)
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (1 x 2)

subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Competition Commission (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Briefly describe the term price leadership.
subQuestions.memoText:
A situation where the dominant business sets the price and the other firms accept it as the market price. (2 marks)
(Accept any other correct relevant response)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the impact of collusion by banks on consumers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any one full explanation:
â€¢ Collusion will result in consumers paying high prices on the banking services.
â€¢ The collusive banks may provide poor quality services to consumers as they will not have any other alternatives.
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Why do businesses aim to achieve economies of scale?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per full explanation (max 4 marks):
â€¢ To reduce the average cost which enables businesses to produce more output.
â€¢ To increase the competitiveness of businesses through lower prices which increase demand.
â€¢ To improve the profitability of businesses due to increased sales / To earn higher profit and expand the investment capacity.
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 x 2)

subQuestions.memoText:

subQuestions.questionText: State a private benefit enjoyed by producers of goods and services.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (any one - 1 mark):

â€¢ Sales revenue

subQuestions.questionText: Briefly describe the term social cost.
subQuestions.memoText:
The total costs of a good or service incurred by the producers and the community at large / Social cost is the sum of private costs and external costs. (2 marks)
(Accept any other correct relevant response)

subQuestions.questionText: Why do positive externalities such as education lead to market failure?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any one full explanation:
â€¢ Goods and services with positive externalities are not highly rated by the market, hence they are under-supplied by markets.
â€¢ Markets tend to produce less quantities of goods with positive externalities because they do not take into account the social benefits.
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: How can the government discourage the consumption of demerit goods?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per full explanation (max 4 marks):
â€¢ The government can increase indirect taxes or excise duties which will increase the price of demerit goods resulting in a decrease in consumption.
â€¢ Awareness campaigns may be created to educate people about the harmful effects of demerit goods.
â€¢ The government can ban the promotion/advertising of demerit goods by producers.
â€¢ Laws can be enforced to regulate the selling of demerit goods, such as tobacco, to people who are under a specific age.
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: With the aid of a correctly-labelled graph, explain the relationship between the demand curve (AR) and the marginal revenue curve of a monopoly.
subQuestions.memoText:
GRAPH (4 marks max):
â€¢ Correct labelling of vertical axis (Price, Revenue) and horizontal axis (Quantity) = 1 mark
â€¢ Correct drawing and labelling of the demand curve (D = AR) = 1 mark
â€¢ Correct drawing and labelling of the marginal revenue curve (MR) = 1 mark
â€¢ Correct positioning of the MR curve in relation to the demand curve (AR) - MR lies below D=AR with MR intersecting the horizontal axis at the midpoint between origin and the AR curve = 1 mark

EXPLANATION (4 marks max - 2 marks per full point):
â€¢ The demand curve (AR) and the marginal revenue (MR) curve for a monopoly are both downward sloping from left to right.
â€¢ The demand curve shows the relation between the price and the quantity demanded while the marginal revenue shows the additional income earned when one additional unit is sold.
â€¢ The marginal revenue (MR) curve is less elastic than the demand curve.
â€¢ The marginal revenue (MR) curve intersects the horizontal axis at the midpoint of the origin and the point of intersection of the demand curve (AR).

Max 4 (graph) + Max 4 (explanation) = 8 marks total

subQuestions.questionText: How can the government redistribute income and wealth to correct market failures?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per full explanation (max 8 marks):
â€¢ A progressive income tax system is used to make higher income earners pay higher tax rate than lower income earners.
â€¢ The government may provide subsidies on goods and services such as housing, education and healthcare to increase affordability for the poor.
â€¢ Welfare or transfer payments such as old-age grants, disability grants and child support grants can be used to provide income to the poor.
â€¢ Tax revenue can be used to provide free services, such as free electricity and water, for the poor people.
â€¢ Implement job creation programmes, such as the Expanded Public Works Programme, to create a source of income for the poor.
â€¢ Intensify the implementation of the Broad Based Black Economic Empowerment Act to accelerate economic transformation for the previously disadvantaged groups.
â€¢ Land reform programmes, such as land restitution and redistribution, can be used to increase the ownership of land amongst the previously disadvantaged groups.
â€¢ Ensure that the Employment Equity Act promotes affirmative action and eliminates discrimination in employment opportunities.
(Accept any other correct relevant response)
(Allocate a maximum of 2 marks for mere listing of facts) (4 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Name any TWO ways used to measure inflation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark per correct way (max 2 marks):
â€¢ Indexes (CPI/PPI)
â€¢ Weighting (Basket of goods and services)
â€¢ Inflation rate

(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: How can the government use education to ensure environmental sustainability?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any one full explanation:
â€¢ Use various methods to create awareness and change people's attitudes towards the environment.
â€¢ Make the society aware of environmental issues and how their actions impact the environment, ensuring better decisions are made.
â€¢ Educate children to be conscious of the effects of their actions on the environment so that they can become more environmentally aware and empowered adults.
â€¢ Setting up community wildlife reserves to educate people about the importance of protecting the environment.
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (1 x 2)

The gradual and continual increase in the earth's average temperature. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Why does the government impose (levy) green taxes on certain goods and services?
subQuestions.memoText:

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the environmental benefits of reducing the use of fossil fuels.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per full explanation (max 4 marks):
â€¢ The amount of carbon emissions in the atmosphere may decrease which reduces the greenhouse effects.

When the economy experiences low economic growth, high unemployment and high inflation at the same time. (2 marks)
(Accept any other correct relevant response)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the behaviour of workers when they expect prices to increase.

(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: How can an increase in interest rates help to combat inflation in the economy?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per full explanation (max 4 marks):
â€¢ The cost of borrowing will increase and reduce excess demand leading to a decrease in demand-pull inflation.
â€¢ Higher interest rates will encourage savings as investors expect higher return on investment which will help curb demand-pull inflation.
â€¢ Higher interest rates may lead to the appreciation of local currency which makes imported production inputs to be cheaper and lower cost-push inflation.
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Briefly discuss conservation and preservation in relation to the state of the environment.
subQuestions.memoText:
CONSERVATION (Max 4 marks - award 2 marks per full point):
â€¢ Conservation relates to the sustainable management of natural resources that are non-renewable to ensure that they are not completely used up and disappear from the environment.
â€¢ Conservation seeks a creative continuity of the environment while ensuring that change is sympathetic to the quality of life for both present and future generations.
â€¢ Conservation is necessary when the stocks of natural resources are utilised more than they can reproduce what has been used.
â€¢ Conservation includes game parks, protected areas for animals and forests, botanical parks, museums, reptile and butterfly sanctuaries.
â€¢ Conservation strategies are employed to ensure sustainable use of natural resources through the utilization of conservation areas.
â€¢ The government can apply different control methods, such as permits and quotas, to conserve natural resources.

PRESERVATION (Max 4 marks - award 2 marks per full point):
â€¢ Preservation refers to keeping resources that are non-renewable intact or unharmed, such as wetlands, an indigenous forest or a river mouth ecosystem.
â€¢ Preservation helps to preserve existing assets to ensure that they do not get used in a way that is destructive to the environment.
â€¢ Preservation involves the elements of the environment that are threatened by extinction, such as Africa's remaining rhino and animal species.
â€¢ Heritage sites that have special cultural or environmental significance are often targeted for preservation.
â€¢ The government may intervene in the market when it is necessary to preserve environmental assets.

(Accept any other correct relevant response)
(Allocate a maximum of 4 marks for mere listing of facts and examples)
(Allocate a maximum of 2 marks for examples only) (2 x 4)

subQuestions.questionText: Analyse the negative impact of high inflation on the South African economy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per full point (max 8 marks):
â€¢ Households may save less as more of their income is used to purchase goods and services when there is high inflation.
â€¢ Consumers' confidence may decrease which may lead to a decline in consumption expenditure.
â€¢ Investments may decrease as high inflation creates a negative sentiment towards the South African economy.
â€¢ High demands for wage increases may lead to an increase in labour costs which reduces production of goods and services.
â€¢ Workers may engage in industrial actions if their wage demands are not met, which may disrupt economic activity.
â€¢ Taxpayers pay higher taxes as their nominal wages increase which shift their income levels into higher tax bracket (bracket creep).
â€¢ Higher inflation results in a decrease in the purchasing power of money leading to the rand buying fewer goods and services than before.
â€¢ Interest rates may increase which leads to an increase in the cost of borrowing money in the economy.
â€¢ High cost of production may force some businesses to reduce their operations which may lead to job losses.
â€¢ High inflation stimulates spending on imported goods and services, as consumers consider them to be cheaper.
â€¢ Increased prices of South African exports may reduce their competitiveness on global markets.
â€¢ The value of local currency may decrease as balance of payments deficit increases.
(Accept any other correct relevant response)
(Allocate a maximum of 2 marks for mere listing of facts) (4 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Why does a monopolistic competitive firm earn normal profit in the long-run?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per full explanation (max 4 marks):
Either set:
â€¢ There are no barriers to entry which allows new businesses to enter the market when there is economic profit.
â€¢ Increase in the number of businesses will increase the market supply and reduce prices until existing firms earn normal profit.
OR
â€¢ The freedom of exit allows some existing businesses to leave the market when there is economic loss.
â€¢ Decrease in the number of businesses will reduce the market supply and increase prices until existing firms earn normal profit.
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Why is core inflation more stable than consumer price index (CPI) inflation?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any one full explanation:
â€¢ Core inflation excludes items that have high volatility in prices and that are regulated by government intervention while the CPI inflation includes items with high volatile prices.
â€¢ Core inflation is not affected by the seasonal variances of food prices while the CPI inflation is affected by seasonal variances of food prices.
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: How can an increase in productivity help to combat inflation?
subQuestions.memoText:

â€¢ The average cost of production will decrease which reduces cost-push inflation.
â€¢ Increases in productivity that are linked to wage increases may neutralise cost-push inflation.
â€¢ Higher productivity through education and training may increase production output which will stimulate aggregate supply.
(Accept any other correct relevant response) (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Briefly discuss productive inefficiency and allocative inefficiency as consequences of market failures.
subQuestions.memoText:
PRODUCTIVE INEFFICIENCY (Max 4 marks - award 2 marks per full point):
â€¢ Occurs when businesses do not maximise output with the available inputs (factors of production).
â€¢ Productive inefficiency means that a business does not produce goods at the lowest possible cost.
â€¢ Productive inefficiency allows businesses to reduce cost without producing fewer goods and lowering quality of goods / There is room for businesses to produce more output at a lower cost.
â€¢ The consequence of productive inefficiency is a loss of output and wasted resources.

ALLOCATIVE INEFFICIENCY (Max 4 marks - award 2 marks per full point):
â€¢ Allocative inefficiency means that the product mix does not reflect consumers' tastes and therefore resources are not allocated in the right proportions.
â€¢ Consumer preferences can be satisfied if businesses can use their resources more efficiently.
â€¢ Supply of goods and services does not correspond with demand as quantities required by consumers are not available, which shows shortage or surplus.
â€¢ Allocative inefficiency occurs when businesses allocate resources inefficiently and produce goods and services that consumers do not want.

(Accept any other correct relevant response)
(Allocate a maximum of 4 marks for mere listing of facts and examples)
(Allocate a maximum of 2 marks for examples only) (2 x 4)

subQuestions.questionText: How can the government use command and control measures to ensure environmental sustainability?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per full point (max 8 marks):
â€¢ The government can impose a range of policies to legislate what people may and may not do.
â€¢ Regulations may be set to enforce environmental limits or standards in terms of how resources may be used.
â€¢ Maximum permitted levels may be set on environmental activities, such as carbon dioxide emissions or resource use.
â€¢ Minimum permitted levels may be imposed on the extraction of resources such as water in reserves and trees in plantation.
â€¢ Quantity standards are set to prescribe the predetermined amount of pollution caused, such as factory and car gas emissions.
â€¢ As technology for reducing pollutants improves, tougher standards can be imposed based on the best available technology.
â€¢ Quality standards are set to prescribe rules and regulations on the environmental impact of pollution emitted.
â€¢ Social impact standards are set to focus on the effect of environmental pollution on people.
â€¢ Tougher standards for noise levels may be imposed in densely populated areas than in rural areas.
â€¢ The government can maintain the stock levels of environmental resources through the issuing of permits/licences and quotas.
â€¢ Inspectors may be assigned to monitor the environmental activities of businesses and compliance to the predetermined standards.
â€¢ Environmental offences can be punishable by law through imposition of fines or withdrawal of permits/licences, quotas and compensation to victims or imprisonment.
â€¢ Direct controls may be used to force offending firms to incur the actual costs of the offending activity.
(Accept any other correct relevant response)
(Allocate a maximum of 2 marks for mere listing of facts) (4 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Essay: 
â€¢ Discuss in detail the short-run equilibrium positions in a perfect market with the aid of three separate graphs. (26 marks)
â€¢ Evaluate the impact of perfect competition on consumers. (10 marks)

Essay structure: Introduction (Max 2), Body Main Part (Max 26), Body Additional Part (Max 10), Conclusion (Max 2). Total: 40 marks.
subQuestions.memoText:
INTRODUCTION (Max 2 marks):
â€¢ A market is a place where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods and services for a price.
â€¢ Perfect competition is a market structure with large numbers of buyers and sellers of homogenous products, and free market entry and exit.
â€¢ Short-run is a period of production in which at least one of the factor inputs is fixed.
(Accept any other relevant introduction)

BODY: MAIN PART (Max 26 marks)

ECONOMIC PROFIT:
Graph (Max 4 marks):
â€¢ Correct labelling of vertical (Price, Cost, Revenue) and horizontal (Quantity) axis = 1 mark
â€¢ Correct drawing and labelling of cost curves (MC, AC) in relation to revenue curves (D=AR=MR) = 1 mark
â€¢ Indication of the economic profit area (between price R20 and AC R15 at output of 100 units) = 1 mark
â€¢ Indication of profit maximization point e (where MR=MC) = 1 mark
Discussion points (2 marks each):
â€¢ Economic profit occurs when total revenue (TR) > total cost (TC) / when AR > AC.
â€¢ Economic profit is the extra profit made in addition to normal profit.
â€¢ At the market price of R20, profit is maximised at point e, where MR = MC.
â€¢ 100 units of the product will be produced at an average cost of R15.
â€¢ The business is making economic profit because the market price is above the AC.
â€¢ When there is economic profit (supernormal profit), new businesses will be attracted to enter the market.
â€¢ The firm makes a total economic profit of R500 (R20 x 100 = R2000 - R15 x 100 = R1500) OR R5 per unit (R20 - R15).

ECONOMIC LOSS:
Graph (Max 4 marks):
â€¢ Correct labelling of vertical and horizontal axis = 1 mark
â€¢ Correct drawing and labelling of cost curves in relation to revenue curves = 1 mark
â€¢ Indication of the economic loss area (between AC R18 and price R15 at output of 100 units) = 1 mark
â€¢ Indication of loss minimization point e (where MR=MC) = 1 mark
Discussion points (2 marks each):
â€¢ Economic loss occurs when TR < TC / when AR < AC.
â€¢ Economic loss is the negative difference between TR and TC.
â€¢ At the market price of R15, loss is minimised at point e, where MR = MC.
â€¢ 100 units of the product will be produced at an average cost of R18.
â€¢ The business is making economic loss because the market price is less than the AC.
â€¢ When there is economic loss, some businesses will leave the market.
â€¢ The firm makes a total economic loss of R300 (R15 x 100 = R1500 - R18 x 100 = R1800) OR R3 loss per unit.

NORMAL PROFIT:
Graph (Max 4 marks):
â€¢ Correct labelling of vertical and horizontal axis = 1 mark
â€¢ Correct drawing and labelling of cost curves in relation to revenue curves = 1 mark
â€¢ Indication of AC equal to the price (D=AR=MR tangent to AC at minimum point) = 1 mark
â€¢ Indication of profit maximization point e (where MR=MC=AC) = 1 mark
Discussion points (2 marks each):
â€¢ Normal profit occurs when TR = TC / when AR = AC.
â€¢ Normal profit is the minimum earnings required to prevent the entrepreneurs from leaving the industry.
â€¢ Normal profit is referred to as ZERO economic profit (break-even) because TR - TC / AR - AC = 0.
â€¢ At the market price of R15, profit is maximised at point e, where MR = MC.
â€¢ 100 units of the product will be produced at an average cost of R15.
â€¢ The business is making normal profit because the market price is equal to the AC.
â€¢ When businesses are making normal profit there will be no incentive for new businesses to enter or existing businesses to leave the market.
â€¢ The firm makes a normal profit of R0 (TR - TC = 0).

(Allocate a maximum of 8 marks for mere listing of facts/examples) (Max 26)

ADDITIONAL PART (Max 10 marks):
Positive impact:
â€¢ Consumers have full information about the prevailing market conditions such as price and quality of the product which helps them make informed decisions.
â€¢ Homogeneous products allow consumers access to products of the same standard (quality).
â€¢ There are many businesses which ensures consumers of adequate availability (supply) of goods and services.
â€¢ Consumers pay lower prices as businesses produce goods at the lowest possible average cost (productive or technical efficiency).
â€¢ Consumers may not be exploited by businesses since collusion is impossible and businesses have no control over the market price.

Negative impact:
â€¢ Consumers' choice and satisfaction may be limited because of homogenous products in the perfect market.
â€¢ Consumers may be confined to lower quality products due to lack of innovation or product development.
â€¢ Consumers may not negotiate for lower price since no individual participant has influence over the market price.
â€¢ Consumers may be exposed to price fluctuations due to entry and exit of suppliers in the market.
(Accept any other correct higher order, relevant response)
(Allocate a maximum of 2 marks for mere listing of facts/examples)

CONCLUSION (Max 2 marks):
In the long-run, a perfectly competitive firm can only make normal profit due to the freedom of entry and exit. / Although perfect competition does not exist in real life, it is necessary to study it to understand an ideal market in which efficiency is achieved.
(Accept any other correct higher order, relevant conclusion)

TOTAL: 40 marks

questions.title: Contemporary Economic Issues - Essay (Section C choice)

subQuestions.questionText:
Essay:
â€¢ Examine in detail the benefits of tourism. (26 marks)
â€¢ Analyse the importance of Indigenous Knowledge Systems (IKS) in promoting tourism. (10 marks)

Essay structure: Introduction (Max 2), Body Main Part (Max 26), Body Additional Part (Max 10), Conclusion (Max 2). Total: 40 marks.
subQuestions.memoText:
INTRODUCTION (Max 2 marks):
Tourism are activities of people travelling to and staying in places outside their usual environment for not more than one consecutive year for leisure, business or other purposes.
(Accept any other correct relevant introduction)

BODY: MAIN PART (Max 26 marks) - Award 2 marks per full point:

HOUSEHOLDS:
â€¢ Members of households earn income directly from the tourism sector as tour operators and travel agents.
â€¢ Many households are indirectly involved in tourism as employees such as in hotels, transport sector.
â€¢ Households that operate as curio producers or musicians can earn income from tourism.
â€¢ A large number of households acquire skills in the tourism industry, e.g. tourism has been introduced as a subject in SA schools since 2000.
â€¢ School curriculum and learnerships can be used to offer households opportunities to acquire skills.
â€¢ Tourism encourages rural development because many tourist attractions are located in rural areas.
â€¢ Local people benefit from improved infrastructure meant for tourists.

BUSINESSES:
â€¢ Tourism stimulates business in areas such as accommodation and entertainment.
â€¢ Manufacturing sector and recreation sector all benefit from increased demand due to tourism.
â€¢ The previously disadvantaged communities get entrepreneurial opportunities through black economic empowerment schemes.
â€¢ A large number of people get business opportunities in the informal sector, such as selling of hand-craft products.
â€¢ Local retailers may have an increase in sales that leads to profits because of increased demand from tourists.
â€¢ Private enterprises and government can form private-public partnerships to provide infrastructure for tourism which increases the income of businesses.
â€¢ Tourism activities encourage businesses to improve the quality and variety of their products.
â€¢ Natural monopolies such as Table Mountain Cableway can achieve abnormal profits from tourism activities.
â€¢ The public sector provides a range of financial incentives, such as grants, subsidies, loans, tax rebates, for private sector tourism investment.

GOVERNMENT:
â€¢ Tourism contributes to the income of the government through:
  - personal income taxes from tourism employees.
  - taxes from tourists such as airport entry/departure taxes, air ticket taxes and taxes on hotel room occupancy.
  - tax revenue from indirect taxes such as VAT and duties on goods and services supplied to tourists.
â€¢ Taxes are charged to recover external costs which is the amount not included in the price.
â€¢ Taxes compensate the host community for providing infrastructure and basic amenities.
â€¢ Tourism is an important foreign exchange earner and boosts the country's foreign exchange reserves.
â€¢ Government is able to achieve socio-economic objectives of informal sector growth, BEE and SMME development.
â€¢ Tourism creates a good image of the country by marketing itself.
â€¢ Government is able to create jobs at a minimum cost.

INFRASTRUCTURE:
â€¢ Adequate and well-maintained infrastructure is essential for tourist destinations.
â€¢ Physical infrastructure such as roads, telecommunications, railway systems, airports and accommodation has been improved and upgraded to meet international standards, e.g. the Gautrain.
â€¢ Local people benefit from the improved infrastructure for tourists, e.g. 2010 World Cup stadiums.
â€¢ Government often prioritises economic infrastructure such as ports and beaches.
â€¢ Social infrastructure such as clinics and hospitals is also important for the growth of tourism.
â€¢ SDIs and development corridors also have tourism as an important focus.
â€¢ Private-partnerships are used for infrastructure development.

(Accept any other correct relevant response)
(Allocate a max of 8 marks for headings/subheadings/examples) (Max 26)

ADDITIONAL PART (Max 10 marks):
â€¢ Indigenous Knowledge Systems (IKS) help to attract tourists as they seek authenticity and uniqueness at local destinations.
â€¢ IKS allow tourists to experience and learn more about South Africa's cultural diversity, indigenous culture, history, environment and how local people live and work.
â€¢ The use of indigenous medicines for health, traditional stories, dances, music, painting, handicraft, hunting and cooking methods attract tourists to local villages.
â€¢ Cultural villages, such as Basotho in the Free State and Simunye Zulu Lodge in KwaZulu-Natal, promote tourism through activities where tour-guides explain and demonstrate storytelling and indigenous knowledge practices.
â€¢ Cultural and township tours, such as Soweto, encourage tourists to experience religious activities, life with local households and eat in township restaurants.
â€¢ World Heritage Sites, such as Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape, Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape, and Robben Island, promote significant cultural and historical aspects of the country.
â€¢ Environmental World Heritage Sites, such as the Cape Fynbos Region, iSimangaliso Wetlands Park and uKhahlamba Drakensberg Park, allow tourists to enjoy South Africa's indigenous environmental uniqueness.
â€¢ Arts and culture festivals, such as the National Arts Festival held annually in Makhanda and the Awesome Africa Music Festival, encourage tourists to visit South Africa.
â€¢ African arts and crafts, such as Maboneng Township Arts Experience in Cape Town, showcase and display local artists and crafters to international tourists.
(Accept any other correct relevant response)
(Allocate a maximum of 2 marks for mere listing of facts/examples)

CONCLUSION (Max 2 marks):
The government should implement suitable strategies that can help promote tourism as it contributes to the gross domestic product and economic growth.
(Accept any other relevant higher order conclusion)

TOTAL: 40 marks
